content.value_statement: Database work slows down when table names and relationships are unclear. This skill maps Empathy Ledger tables and provides Supabase query patterns for faster planning.
actual_capabilities: Identifies core Empathy Ledger tables and their documented purposes.
Maps foreign-key relationships across tenants, profiles, projects, stories, transcripts, and media.
Shows documented SQL patterns for story counts, themes, and frequency analysis.
Provides Supabase select patterns for nested story, transcript, and organisation data.
Highlights tenant filtering as a required query constraint.
limitations: The reference describes Empathy Ledger and is not a general Supabase schema guide.
It does not connect to a database or execute queries.
The documented schema may differ from the current deployed database.
Generated queries still require review for permissions, RLS policies, and production performance.

use_cases.title: Find analysis data
use_cases.description: Locate stories, transcripts, themes, and extracted quotes before planning reports or research.

use_cases.title: Plan application queries
use_cases.description: Trace table relationships and select suitable joins for Supabase application features.

use_cases.title: Review tenant boundaries
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed data path includes the documented tenant relationship and filtering pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Identify relevant tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Which Empathy Ledger tables contain stories, transcripts, themes, and quotes? Explain each table's role.

prompt_templates.title: Map a relationship path
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the relationship from an organisation to its projects, stories, storytellers, and media. List the required joins.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a tenant-aware query
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Supabase query for published stories with storyteller and project details. Include tenant filtering and explain each relationship.

prompt_templates.title: Review a complex data workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed story distribution workflow against the documented schema. Identify missing tenant, consent, audit, token, or relationship checks: [workflow].

output_examples.input: Which tables support story theme analysis?
output_examples.output: Use stories for core content, story_themes for associations, narrative_themes for theme definitions, and transcript_analysis_results for versioned analysis.

output_examples.input: How does an organisation connect to published stories?
output: Join projects through the organisation relationship.
Filter by tenant and published status.

output_examples.input: What should I check before querying stories?
output_examples.output: Confirm the current schema, apply tenant filtering, respect RLS policies, select only required fields, and review access to storyteller and media data.

best_practices: Verify table and column names against the current deployed schema before implementation.
Apply tenant constraints and rely on reviewed RLS policies for every data path.
Select only required fields and test nested joins with realistic access roles.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the reference as proof that a table or relationship still exists.
Do not omit tenant filtering because an example query appears simple.
Do not expose sensitive profile, transcript, token, or audit data without authorization review.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to Supabase?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and query planning guidance without opening a database connection.

faq.question: Is this a general Supabase skill?
faq.answer: No. Its table names and relationships are specific to the Empathy Ledger application.

faq.question: Can it generate queries?
faq.answer: It can help draft SQL and Supabase query patterns from the documented relationships.

faq.question: Does it guarantee tenant isolation?
faq.answer: No. Developers must verify filters, authorization checks, and active RLS policies in the deployed environment.

faq.question: Does it include every database table?
faq.answer: It includes the tables and relationships present in its bundled references, which may not match the live schema.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
